vocabulary.meaning_en: (business) an activity or part of a company that is working; (medicine) surgery on a patient
when a doctor cuts open the body to repair it
(medicine) to lose a lot of blood; (business) to lose a lot of money

vocabulary.note_en: A brand name used as a general word.
vocabulary.example: Put a Band-Aid on your finger.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (business) a quick, temporary fix that doesn't solve the real problem
vocabulary.example: Band-Aid solutions never work for long.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (medicine) a liquid mixture; (business) a way to deal with a difficult problem
vocabulary.example: We need a real solution to this problem.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an amount of medicine taken at one time
vocabulary.note_ar: a dose of strong medicine = إجراء قاسٍ لكنه ضروري
vocabulary.note_en: a dose of strong medicine = a hard but needed action
vocabulary.example: The company needs a dose of strong medicine.

vocabulary.meaning_en: dead on arrival; (business) a plan that fails before it starts
vocabulary.meaning_ar: متوفّى عند الوصول / مشروع فاشل منذ البداية
vocabulary.example: Without money, the deal was DOA.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to let someone into a hospital as a patient
vocabulary.example: He was admitted to hospital last night.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a medical examination to check your health
vocabulary.example: I have a dental checkup next week.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to check how someone or something is doing
vocabulary.example: Check up on him by the end of the week.

vocabulary.meaning_en: deciding who or what needs help first, based on how serious it is
vocabulary.example: We need to triage these problems: the lawsuit comes first.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the need to deal with something quickly
vocabulary.example: Patients are seen in order of urgency.

vocabulary.meaning_en: do not resuscitate; (business, joke) a career or project that will never be saved
vocabulary.meaning_ar: عدم الإنعاش / انتهاء مسيرة بلا رجعة
vocabulary.example: After the scandal, they put a DNR on his career.
This lesson tests your listening comprehension.

fine_lines.title: checkup vs check up on
fine_lines.explanation_ar: checkup (كلمة واحدة) اسم: فحص طبي. check up on (كلمات منفصلة) فعل: يتفقّد شخصًا أو شيئًا.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Checkup (one word) is a noun: a medical exam. Check up on (separate) is a verb: to see how someone is doing.

examples.sentence: I have my yearly checkup tomorrow.
I'll check up on the car repair later.

fine_lines.title: Band-Aid solution vs real solution
fine_lines.explanation_ar: Band-Aid solution حلّ مؤقت صغير لا يعالج أصل المشكلة. solution حلّ حقيقي.
fine_lines.explanation_en: A Band-Aid solution is a small temporary fix. A solution really solves the problem.

examples.sentence: Borrowing more money is just a Band-Aid solution.
The real solution is to cut costs.

expressions.meaning_en: It is losing a lot of money.
expressions.example: The new branch is hemorrhaging money.
The company needs a dose of strong medicine.
Their offer was dead on arrival.

expressions.meaning_en: Waiting calmly helps more than anything.
expressions.example: Keep studying; patience is the best medicine.

questions.question: "The ___ was a success, and the woman got a new heart."
"The difficult problem has two possible ___."
questions.explanation_en: Solutions = ways to deal with a problem.

questions.question: "___ solutions never work over a long period." (temporary)
"The ___ of medicine was too high." (amount at one time)
A business plan that fails as soon as it is mentioned is ___.
"Call the mechanic and ___ the car." (see how it's going)
questions.explanation_en: Check up on = see how it's doing.

questions.question: Deciding which problem to fix first, by how serious it is, is ___.
"You can't put a ___ on a broken heart." (small bandage)
questions.explanation_en: A Band-Aid is a small bandage.
